explanation: A moray shoots a second set of jaws forward from its throat, grabs the prey and drags it down, much like the inner jaws of the creature in the film Alien.

claims.text: Moray eels use a second set of jaws in the throat (pharyngeal jaws) to pull prey into the gullet.
Moray eels do not pull prey into the gullet with a sticky tongue, strong suction or hooked gill rakers.
A moray's pharyngeal jaws move forward from the throat to grab prey and pull it down.
The creature in the film Alien has a second, inner jaw that shoots out of its mouth.
